The user says "I need to arrange a flight on booking number 1234 as soon as possible." That could mean they want to change the flight details for booking 1234.

But the user also wants to check different options: "Calculate the fare from the first airport in the available list to the last airport in the same list, on the last day of October 2024, in business class."

So we need to get the list of all airports. Then pick the first and last. Then get flight cost for that route on 2024-10-31 business class. Then provide estimated total payable amount. But what about the booking number 1234? We might need to cancel it? Or just book a new flight? The user says "arrange a flight on booking number 1234 as soon as possible." That could mean they want to book a flight under that booking number. But booking numbers are usually assigned after booking. So maybe they want to create a new booking with that ID? Not sure.

We can interpret that they want to book a flight for booking number 1234. But we don't have an access token yet. We need to authenticate. The user hasn't provided credentials. We need to ask for them. But the user didn't give us client_id, client_secret, etc. We cannot proceed until we have an access token. So we need to ask the user for their credentials or at least confirm that we have them. Alternatively, we can call get_all_credit_cards to see if we have any. But we still need an access token.

Thus we need to ask the user for their credentials (client_id, client_secret, refresh_token, grant_type, user_first_name, user_last_name). But the user didn't provide them. So we need to ask for them.

Also, we need to get the list of airports. That requires no auth. So we can call list_all_airports. Then compute flight cost. Then we can estimate total payable amount. But we also need to know the user's credit card balance to ensure they can pay. But the user didn't specify a card. We can ask for card id. But we can also get all credit cards. But we need an access token.

Thus we need to authenticate first. So we ask the user for credentials.
